reason: I’ll supply the muscle fibers with sugar toward the fuel and oxygen goal; it’s the only offered action.
expectation: The fibers will receive sugar, and oxygen may be needed next.

effect: Sugar is processed in the cell fluid, producing some ATP and fuel that enters a mitochondrion; oxygen is the next available addition.
reaction: The separate arrows are a little unclear without more explanation, but I’m curious what oxygen adds.
reason: I’ll add oxygen to advance the supply goal; it’s the only offered combination.
expectation: The fibers will use oxygen with the processed fuel, likely supporting more ATP production.

effect: Oxygen and fuel support ATP production in mitochondria, and ATP powers muscle work. The next goal is to collect and transmit the fibers’ pulls.
reaction: The ATP cycle makes the running cost clearer, though ADP has not been explained.
reason: I’ll add the wrapping to group the fibers; it’s the only offered combination.
expectation: The wrapping will bundle the muscle fibers so their pulls can be collected.

effect: The wrapping grouped the muscle cells into bundles, with their attachment ends still awaiting tendons.
reaction: The shared sleeve makes the grouping clear; I’m curious how the two tendon sets relate.
reason: I’ll add the front tendons to start transmitting the bundles’ pull; either tendon set appears available.
expectation: The front tendons will attach to the bundles, forming a muscle group that can transmit force.

alternatives.reason: The rear tendons also seem suitable, but I chose to start with the front set.

effect: The front tendons formed bending muscles and will need an attachment to move a joint.
reaction: The tendon’s role is clear, and I’m curious how the rear group will work with it.
reason: I’ll add the rear tendons to make the other muscle group; it’s the only offered combination.
expectation: The rear tendons will form a second muscle group, perhaps one that straightens the joint.

effect: The rear tendons formed straightening muscles, completing the goal of collecting and transmitting the fibers’ pulls.
reaction: The paired bending and straightening groups make sense, though I would like to see how they attach to bones.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen was most worthwhile because the result connected fuel and oxygen to ATP production and muscle work.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding sugar was less clear: the separate arrows showed ATP and processed fuel, but did not explain their relationship much.

surprise.text: I was interested that the cells keep remaking ATP as muscles use it; the picture made the continuing energy cost clearer, though ADP was unexplained.

arbitrary.text: Choosing front before rear tendons felt somewhat arbitrary because both were offered and I had no reason to prefer that order.

continue.text: Yes. I would choose to continue to see how the two muscle groups attach to bones and move a joint.
